Application Materials.content:
As part of your application, you must provide the following supporting documents:
- **Your official transcript.** Please read UCL’s guide on [getting your academic transcript](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/getting-your-academic-transcript "Getting your academic transcript").
- **A personal statement.** UCL’s [personal statement guidance](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/writing-your-personal-statement "Writing your personal statement") offers advice on writing an effective personal statement.
- If you need a visa to study at UCL, you will need to provide a copy of your current **passport**. If you do not have a valid passport, you can complete the Missing passport document and provide your passport later.
- Some courses require additional documents as part of the application. Full details can be found on UCL’s [additional course requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/degree-types/courses-additional-requirements "Courses with additional requirements") page.
- If you meet UCL’s [English language requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/english-language-requirements "English Language requirements") using a UCL-recognised test, you should upload your official test report form or qualification. If you cannot provide this evidence when you submit your application, your application will still be considered.
The number of references needed to support your application can be found on the prospectus page for your course. You should read UCL’s guidance on [selecting your reference](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/selecting-your-references "Selecting your references") and contact your nominated referee(s) before starting your application to check they can provide a reference for you.
Do **not** password-protect or encrypt files. Before submitting, make sure you have uploaded the correct version of each supporting document, that your official transcripts clearly show your name, institution, modules and any grades received, that you have provided accurate details of any work experience or previous employment either in the employment section or uploaded CV, that you have uploaded any compulsory supporting documents required for your course, and that any referee details use institutional or professional email addresses. You cannot replace or add additional documents once you have submitted your application.

Application Deadlines.content:
Programme starts **September 2026**.
Applications accepted:
- Applicants who require a visa: **20 Oct 2025 – 26 Jun 2026**. Applications close at **5pm UK time**.
- Applicants who do not require a visa: **20 Oct 2025 – 28 Aug 2026**. Applications close at **5pm UK time**.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **A minimum of an upper second-class Bachelor's degree** or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard.
- This course is suitable for those with **a quantitative background** who have an interest in energy and are motivated by using data science to solve sustainability problems; those with **an energy background** who are interested in data science; and **early and mid-career energy professionals** looking to expand their data skills and domain knowledge.
- For applicants from China: **a four-year bachelor’s degree from a recognised Chinese higher education institution** will be considered. The required grade will vary depending on the awarding university.
- For applicants from UCL's reviewed list of Chinese universities, which includes a selection of Project 211, Project 985, and Double First-Class universities: for an **Upper second-class (2:1)** requirement, a Bachelor's degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 85%** is required. Not all universities from these projects are included.
- For applicants from all other universities recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education: for an **Upper second-class (2:1)** requirement, a Bachelor's degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 90%** is required.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
The English language level for Energy Systems and Data Analytics (ESDA) MSc is: **Level 2**. [UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses) are for international students aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL.
- **IELTS Academic:** **overall score of 7.0 and a minimum of 6.5 in each component**. IELTS Academic Online is accepted; IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted.
- **TOEFL iBT, tests taken from 21 January 2026:** **overall score of 4.5 and 4.5 in reading, writing, speaking and listening**.
- **TOEFL iBT, tests taken before 21 January 2026:** **overall score of 96 with 24/30 in reading and writing and 22/30 in speaking and listening**. TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition is accepted; TOEFL iBT MyBestScore is not acceptable. UCL’s institution code for TOEFL is **9163**.
- **Cambridge English: C2 Proficiency (CPE):** **overall score of 180 with 172 in all subtests**.
- **Cambridge English: C1 Advanced (CAE):** **overall score of 180 with 172 in all subtests**.
- **Pearson Test of English (Academic):** **overall score of 76 with a minimum of 75 in each Communicative Skill**.

Program Overview.content:
Energy Systems and Data Analytics (ESDA) MSc is based in London, Bloomsbury. The programme equips students with advanced data science, artificial intelligence and energy modelling skills to address complex challenges in the energy transition and prepares them for careers in energy analytics, policy, consulting, or smart technology development.
Designed in collaboration with industry, the degree combines technical knowledge of energy systems with expertise in data science and AI. Students develop expertise to:
- Use data science, machine learning and AI to extract insights from large and diverse datasets.
- Analyse complex energy systems, including supply, demand, sector interdependencies, and infrastructure planning.
- Apply modelling tools to support decarbonisation, smart grid optimisation and low-carbon transitions.
- Evaluate and deploy methods in supervised and unsupervised learning, deep learning and predictive analytics.
- Work with spatial data to understand the geographic and place-based dimensions of energy systems.
The course is suitable for those with a quantitative background who have an interest in energy and are motivated by using data science to solve sustainability problems; those with an energy background who are interested in data science; and early and mid-career energy professionals looking to expand their data skills and domain knowledge.
Study mode is full-time, part-time, or flexible. Duration is 1 calendar year full-time, 2 calendar years part-time, or 5 calendar years flexible. Students undertake modules to the value of 180 credits. Upon successful completion of 180 credits, students are awarded an MSc in Energy Systems and Data Analytics (ESDA); 120 credits leads to a PG Dip; and 60 credits leads to a PG Cert.
Learning takes place at the [UCL Energy Institute](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/bartlett/environment-energy-resources/energy), part of [The Bartlett School of Environment, Energy and Resources](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/bartlett/environment-energy-resources), where experts shape policy, drive innovation and collaborate with industry across the energy sector. Students benefit from a learning environment grounded in real-world challenges and live research, guest lectures and practitioner input across government, industry, consultancy, and the non-profit sector, close links to London’s energy, climate and data sectors, and opportunities to collaborate on applied projects and build a professional network.
Teaching and learning methods include lectures, workshops, hands-on practical sessions, collaborative projects, and self-directed study. Assessment includes problem sets, individual assignments and coursework, group-based data analysis assignments with a report and presentation, unseen examinations and a dissertation. Full-time students study eight taught modules across Term 1 and Term 2, then complete the dissertation during Term 3 and the summer. Part-time students take the taught modules over two years and complete the dissertation in Term 3 of the final year. Flexible students have up to five years to complete eight taught modules.
100% of Energy Systems and Data Analytics MSc graduates were in employment or further study within 15 months of graduation ([HESA Graduate Outcomes Survey 2019-23](https://public.tableau.com/app/profile/katy.coyte4085/viz/WhatDoUCLGraduatesDo/WhatdoUCLgraduatesdo)). Graduates have gone on to careers in government, consultancy, energy utilities, data and AI start-ups, and global NGOs. Typical roles include energy analysts, data scientists, sustainability consultants, and climate policy advisors. Notable employers include Octopus Energy, Deloitte, Shell, China Huadian, and Atkins. Many graduates also pursue advanced research opportunities and PhD study at institutions including UCL.
The course develops technical and analytical skills sought in the Net Zero workforce, including hands-on experience in data science, machine learning, and energy systems modelling using real-world energy datasets; expertise in Python, data visualisation, and statistical analysis tailored to energy applications; the ability to interpret and communicate technical insights for energy policy and business decisions; and critical problem-solving skills through interdisciplinary, research-led teaching and group project work.
The Energy Systems and Data Analytics MSc is affiliated with the Energy Institute (EI) through its Learning Affiliate (LA) scheme, giving students free EI membership during their studies and access to professional development resources, industry networks, and sector events. The LA status supports the course’s current pursuit of full professional accreditation by the EI.
The course offers networking opportunities through events with fellow students, alumni, faculty, and industry experts, plus guest lectures and seminars with industry leaders. Its London location provides access to industry events, exhibitions, and conferences.

Curriculum.content:
Study mode: Full-time, Part-time, Flexible. Duration: Full-time **1 calendar year**; Part-time **2 calendar years**; Flexible **5 calendar years**. Programme starts September 2026.
Teaching and learning methods include lectures, workshops, hands-on practical sessions, collaborative projects, and self-directed study. Assessment is through problem sets, individual assignments and coursework, group-based data analysis assignments with a report and presentation, unseen examinations and a dissertation. Full-time students typically engage in 8 to 15 contact hours per week in Terms 1 and 2, with Term 3 dedicated to independent dissertation research.
Modules:
- Full-time: You take eight taught modules across Term 1 and Term 2. You complete the dissertation during Term 3 and the summer, having had preparatory tutorials during the previous terms. You take seven compulsory modules and choose one optional module.
- Part-time: You take eight taught modules across Term 1 and Term 2 over two years. You complete the dissertation during Term 3 of your final year. You take seven compulsory modules and choose one optional module.
- Flexible: As a flexible student you have up to five years to complete eight taught modules. You take seven compulsory modules and also choose one optional module.
Compulsory modules:
- [Energy Systems](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-systems-BENV0090)
- [Advanced Machine Learning for Energy Systems](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/advanced-machine-learning-for-energy-systems-BENV0148)
- [Energy Data Analysis](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-data-analysis-BENV0091)
- [Statistics for Energy Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/statistics-for-energy-analytics-BENV0094)
- [Energy Data Analytics in the Built Environment](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-data-analytics-in-the-built-environment-BENV0092)
- [Energy and Transport Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-and-transport-analytics-BENV0095)
- [Dissertation: Energy Systems and Data Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/dissertation-energy-systems-and-data-analytics-BENV0096)
- [Spatial Analysis of Energy Data](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/spatial-analysis-of-energy-data-BENV0093)
Optional modules:
- UK Energy and Environment Policy and Law
- [Energy, Technology and Innovation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-technology-and-innovation-BENV0016)
- [Systems Thinking and System Dynamics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/systems-thinking-and-system-dynamics-BENV0047)
- [International Commodity Trade](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/international-commodity-trade-BENV0074)
- [Econometrics of Energy Markets](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/econometrics-of-energy-markets-BENV0122)
- [Electricity Market Design for the Energy Transition](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/electricity-market-design-for-the-energy-transition-BENV0185)
- [Applied Bayesian Methods](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/applied-bayesian-methods-STAT0031)
Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of **180 credits**, you will be awarded an MSc in Energy Systems and Data Analytics (ESDA).

Financial Aid.content:
- Spärck AI Scholarship: UK Government award supporting talented leaders in AI and its application across diverse disciplines.
- **Value:** Full tuition fees plus £22,780 stipend (for one year).
- **Available to:** Prospective students.
- **Selection criteria:** Academic Merit; strengths and motivations, prioritizing underrepresented groups.
- **Eligible fee status:** Home and Overseas.
- **Eligible programmes:** Selected 1-year full-time Master's programmes, including [MSc Energy Systems and Data Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/taught-degrees/energy-systems-and-data-analytics-esda-msc).
- **Deadline:** **17:00 (BST), Friday 1st May 2026.**
- Candidates must have submitted a complete admission application, including references, for a full-time Master's degree at UCL starting in 2026/27 in an eligible programme.
- There are up to 100 scholarships available across all nine participating UK universities in 2026/27. UCL has 8 scholarships to award in total.
- The scholarship is tenable for one year only and may not be held alongside other UK Government scholarships, studentships, awards, or bursaries.
- To apply, applicants should already have received an offer of admission from one of the participating programmes, complete the [Sparck AI Scholarship Application Form](https://view.officeapps.live.com/op/view.aspx?src=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ucl.ac.uk%2Fscholarships%2Fsites%2Fscholarships%2Ffiles%2Fsparck_ai_application_form.docx&wdOrigin=BROWSELINK), obtain a reference letter using the [Reference Guidance - Sparck AI Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/sites/scholarships/files/sparck_ai_scholarship_reference_document.pdf), and email the completed application form and reference by **17:00(BST), Friday 1st May 2026.**
| Programme | Application submission email address |
| --- | --- |
| MSc Energy Systems and Data Analytics | [bartlett.pg-bseer@ucl.ac.uk](mailto:bartlett.pg-bseer@ucl.ac.uk "mailto:bartlett.pg-bseer@ucl.ac.uk") |
- Interviews for shortlisted candidates are expected to be held in **early June 2026**; scholarship offers in **mid to late June 2026**; offers must be accepted by **mid-July 2026** at the latest. Scholarships are for study only in the academic year 2026-27 and cannot be deferred.

Multiple Applications.content:
You may submit applications for a maximum of **two** taught graduate courses for entry to the 2026/27 academic year. The applications must be for different courses. If an application fee is charged, it will be charged per application. UCL does not accept multiple applications for the same course in the same academic year.
If you apply for more than one course the fee is payable for each application that requires an application fee.
If you would like to apply for a different course, you will need to submit a new application for the course you wish to be considered for. Please be aware that you may submit applications for a maximum of two graduate courses for entry to the 2025/26 academic year.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer. However, UCL will consider a request to defer only in exceptional circumstances outside of your control, including:
- The serious illness of the offer holder or the serious illness of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The death of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The need to take parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months.
- Where the offer holder is directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster, such as war, earthquakes or flooding.
- The offer holder has been awarded a UCL scholarship, including UCL partnership agreements and Faculty awards, or a full scholarship from a recognised funding body for study in the following academic year.
To be eligible for a deferral you must hold an unconditional offer which you have accepted. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt, if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme. If you wish to defer but do not fall into one of the permitted categories, you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, but applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake.
To request a deferral, you must do so on the offer page of your application portal. If requesting a deferral due to illness or parental or adoption leave, you must provide a letter from a relevant medical practitioner. If requesting a deferral on the basis of a scholarship for study in the following academic year, you must upload a copy of your official scholarship award letter. UCL reserves the right to request more information before making a final decision.
An application cannot be deferred twice. Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants.
The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
If a deferral request is approved, any tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment. You will receive a new offer letter and may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- The offer page of the applicant portal and the offer letter will clearly outline if the offer is conditional and what conditions must be met.
- Offer holders must accept their offer to upload documents to clear condition(s), and documentary evidence must be uploaded through the Document Uploads section of the [applicant portal](https://evision.ucl.ac.uk/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn); UCL cannot accept documents provided by offer holders through email.
- If a degree condition has not been met, applicants should upload evidence of their degree and final grade to the [applicant portal](https://evision.ucl.ac.uk/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn) so UCL can review them.
- For standard **28 September** starters, conditional offer holders must provide documentary evidence to clear condition(s) by **11 September 2026**. Documents provided after this date will be considered on a case-by-case basis and at UCL’s discretion. For all other start dates, applicants should check the offer letter for the deadline that applies to the course.
- Applicants who need to take a UCL accepted English language test are strongly encouraged to book a test as soon as possible.
- International students holding a conditional offer will be asked to confirm that the details UCL holds are correct and supply anything incorrect or missing. Upon receipt of responses and once the offer is unconditional firm, UCL will aim to issue the CAS as soon as possible.
- Pre-enrolment invitations can only be sent once the applicant has accepted the offer and met any conditions.
